clinician.final_diagnosis: Anorectal malignant melanoma metastatic to the breast
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 63-year-old woman presented with intermittent blood in the stool for 2 months and was diagnosed with anorectal malignant melanoma in February 2019, confirmed by surgical resection and immunohistochemistry (HMB-45, Melan-A, S100, Vimentin positive; PCK, P16 negative). Approximately 29 months later, a new neoplastic lump was identified in her right breast during a staging CT scan. A biopsy of this breast lesion confirmed a malignant tumor. Immunohistochemical staining of the breast lesion showed HMB-45, Melan-A, S100, Vimentin positive, and CK, CK7, CD34, WT-1 negative, consistent with metastatic melanoma. A modified radical mastectomy was performed, and histology confirmed metastatic malignant melanoma.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with intermittent blood in the stool for 2 months and was diagnosed with anorectal malignant tumor in February 2019.
Surgical resection and histology of the anorectal tumor confirmed malignant melanoma, with IHC showing HMB-45 (+), Melan-A (+), S100 (+), Vimentin (+), PCK (-), P16 (-).
Approximately 29 months later, a new lump (2.3 cm nodules, neoplastic lesions) was noted in the outer upper quadrant of the right breast during a CT scan for staging purposes.
Biopsy of the breast lesion revealed findings consistent with malignant tumor.
Immunohistochemical staining of the breast lesion showed HMB-45 (+), Melan-A (+), S100 (+), Vimentin (+), CK (-), CK7 (-), CD34 (-), WT-1 (-), confirming metastatic malignant melanoma.
A modified radical mastectomy was performed for the breast lesion, and histology confirmed it was metastatic malignant melanoma.
